instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Choose What Matters More
cards.instruction: Make someone choose between emotional safety and the outcome they claim to want.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They're calling your number. Chin up, as we practised. Are you going to let them hear the voice I've spent two years dragging out of you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I want the part. I don't want them laughing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then choose which one we're working on. I can walk you in, or drive you home with your pride untouched.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Walk me in, but promise they won't laugh.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. I taught you to project, not to control the room. I'll stay beside the door. Is that enough to get you through it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we renew the lease, ask whether I want to live together. Remember our practice conversations? I kept stopping you from putting my answer in the question.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I want your honest answer. Just don't say anything that makes me panic.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good start, then you added the old condition. We can have the truth or a quiet dinner. Which do you want?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The truth. But start by saying we're fine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There it is again. Take 'we're fine' out and ask me. Or pick up the menu; I'll wait while you choose.

cards.title: Stay for the Hard Part
cards.instruction: Create increasing moments of emotional honesty to test whether someone remains present and supportive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave the laptop shut a minute. Remember how I made you listen to a whole problem before fixing it? I haven't booked our anniversary trip.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought you just needed help with the flights.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I let you think that. I was relieved when the cheap seats sold out. Don't reach for another solution yet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I won't. Is it the trip, or us?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Us. You finally asked the difficult question. I was hoping the trip would fall through. Can you stay beside me while I say the rest?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I wasn't just late to the reunion. Remember when I coached your interviews? Let me finish an answer before you help me with it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I saved you a seat. Was it the traffic?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There's that helpful answer. No. I waited outside for half an hour. Can you stay for the less sensible bit?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm here. I thought you didn't want to sit with me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I did. I thought you'd enjoy yourself more if I stayed outside. Don't tidy that up for me. Just sit beside me now, if you still want to.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Drop the Armor
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to lower their guard, stop performing strength, or admit what affects them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Shop's locked. Lose the customer voice. I taught you that smile for selling shoes, not for talking to me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Someone has to keep morale up. You're my only employee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And you're still doing the trainee smile when you're frightened. I'm off the clock. What happened after you counted the till?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I cried in the stockroom. Then I practised smiling.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You never used to practise anything that hard. Come out here with me next time. You don't have to get your face right first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Over dinner, all you've told me is that you're 'managing'. That's the perfect-host voice I taught you. What's hard about going home?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The silence. I leave the television on so it sounds occupied.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then invite someone who can answer. You mastered the place settings years ago; you can ask me without planning a meal.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll cook. I promise I won't be miserable all evening.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the bit you can unlearn. Invite me while you're miserable. We can make toast, and you needn't apologise for it.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: I Started the Spiral
cards.instruction: Hide how much your own fear or resentment created the emotional crisis while helping everyone calm it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's reassure the stallholders the fair's still on. Write one of those calm updates we practised—no panic in the first sentence.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You panicked about the forecast and told them to cancel their vans.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And now I've got everyone on one contact list. Start with 'The fair is going ahead'. You used to bury the useful news.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Two vans are cancelled because of you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll find replacements. Good updates say what's being done, remember? Call it a transport hiccup, then put my replacement offer in bold.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The club money's in the other envelope. Give everyone the corrected balance. You know how I drilled accuracy into you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You phoned me crying that the treasurer had stolen it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So now you have better information. You're usually good at replacing an old figure with a new one; do that with this message.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I told the whole committee what you said.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Very thorough. Get them on one call; I'll explain the envelopes. Introduce it as a balance update. Leave the crying out—you used to put far too much colour in your reports.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Not the Real Fear
cards.instruction: Keep the conversation focused on practical details so no one reaches the fear underneath them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I open the scholarship letter, make the tea properly. Warm the pot first—how many times did we practise that?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've made yours. Open it; I want to know if you're leaving.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've put sugar in. You always got eager and skipped the asking. I'll need another cup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Take mine. Are you frightened of going, or staying here with me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't give me yours and leave yourself nothing. Make a fresh one. Measure the leaves this time; I'll watch so you don't have to guess.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we discuss me moving out, check my train time. You remember our first trips? I had to make you read the small print.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Six twelve. I've checked five times. Your ticket's in your hand.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good checking. Now the barrier: does this work, or do I need the booking email? Don't assume the big print tells us everything.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll walk you through. Are you scared of leaving me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then check whether you need a ticket for the platform. You always forgot the part that applied to you. We should get that straight first.
